title: Authentication and Authorization Vulnerabilities
learning_outcomes: Explain what authentication and authorization vulnerabilities contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: broken access controls.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. In this lesson, focus on broken access controls; then compare it with insecure session handling. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use authentication and authorization vulnerabilities when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. For authentication and authorization vulnerabilities, begin with broken access controls. Also distinguish insecure session handling; credential abuse; object-level permission checks. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Validate data at system boundaries and encode output for the target context; validation and escaping solve different problems.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for authentication and authorization vulnerabilities from top to bottom. Start by identifying broken access controls, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.
